docs.title: esMorph
docs.text:
esMorph is a morphological analyzer of Spanish: a Rust core with a Python API. For a word form the analyzer finds its analyses in a dictionary built from Wiktionary - the lemma, the part of speech and the Universal Dependencies features - orders them by probability and builds the forms of the word: conjugation, gender and number.

Early version

Before 1.0 the API may change between 0.x versions; the changes are described in the release notes.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Analysis

    Lemma, UD part of speech and features, probability of the analysis; the analysis of a sentence in context, lists of words, lemmatization and documents of the anySeg segmenter without the GIL

  • Universal Dependencies

    Parts of speech, features and lemmas by the UD guidelines and the AnCora conventions; verbs with clitics, numbers, signs and names by rules, unknown words by their ending

    Word analysis

  • Inflection

    Forms of the lexeme and the form by UD features: conjugation, gender and number

    Inflection

  • Command line

    The esmorph command: lemmas, CoNLL-U, TSV or JSON Lines of text, tokens or CoNLL-U files

    The esmorph command

  • spaCy

    The esmorph component: the analysis in context in place of the tagger, the morphologizer and the lemmatizer of a pipeline

    spaCy

  • Comparison

    Accuracy, inflection and speed compared with simplemma, spaCy, Stanza, ablaut and verbecc, loading and memory

    Comparison

  • Exceptions

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
Python 3.11 or newer is required.

pip install esmorph

Prebuilt wheels, building from source and the Rust crate are described on the Installation page.

Project structure
  • crates/esmorph - the Rust core of the analyzer: dictionary format, building, analysis, rules, guessing and inflection
  • crates/esmorph-build - building the dictionary from the export of Wiktionary and the counts of the treebanks
  • crates/esmorph-dict-es - the crate with the dictionary for esmorph on crates.io
  • crates/esmorph-py - the Python module esmorph._esmorph on PyO3
  • python/esmorph - the Python package
  • scripts - exporting Wiktionary and the counts of the treebanks, the conventions of the dictionary, training the context model, checking the installed package before publishing and the comparison with other tools
  • data - the tables of closed classes after UD Spanish AnCora and of the symbols of units, the weights of the context model
  • docs - MkDocs documentation in English and Spanish
  • tests - tests of the Python package

docs.title: Word analysis
docs.text:
An analysis is an Analysis object returned by the analyze and analyze_many methods of the analyzer: the lemma, the part of speech and the Universal Dependencies features, the probability, the words of the token and the source of the analysis. Analyses are immutable; they can be compared (the probability takes no part in the comparison, so an analysis equals its form from forms()), put into sets and pickled. The forms of a word are given by the forms and inflect methods - see Inflection.

CodeResult 
from esmorph import Analyzer

morph = Analyzer()
analysis = morph.analyze("cantaban")[0]
analysis.word, analysis.lemma, analysis.pos, analysis.feats, analysis.words, analysis.source

('cantaban',
 'cantar',
 'VERB',
 {'Mood': 'Ind', 'Number': 'Plur', 'Person': '3', 'Tense': 'Imp', 'VerbForm': 'Fin'},
 ('cantaban',),
 'dictionary')

docs.title: Attributes
docs.text: Attribute Type Description word str The word form as the dictionary spells it, with its accents; a verb with clitics as written, in lower case; a token of the rules as written, without invisible characters, with combining marks joined to their letters and with - for the hyphens U+2010 and U+2011 lemma str The lemma pos str UD part of speech: NOUN, VERB, ADJ, DET, ADP and so on feats dict[str, str] UD features: {"Gender": "Fem", "Number": "Plur"}; a new dictionary each time, changing it does not change the analysis prob float Share of the analysis among the analyses of the word; it sums to 1 over all of them. From analyze_sentence - the score of the context model in the sentence words tuple[str, ...] Words of the token: a verb and its clitics, the words of a contraction (del, al, the older desta), or the word itself; the analysis describes the first of them source str Where the analysis comes from: "dictionary" - the word form is in the dictionary, "clitics" - a verb of the dictionary with clitics, "rule" - an analysis by rule, "guess" - a guessed analysis of an unknown word

docs.title: Parts of speech and features
docs.text:
Parts of speech, features and lemmas follow the Universal Dependencies guidelines and, where they are silent, the conventions of the largest Spanish treebank, UD Spanish AnCora, so the output can be compared with spaCy, Stanza and other UD tools:

  • determiners, pronouns, prepositions and conjunctions have the lemmas and features of AnCora: la is the article el (Definite=Def, PronType=Art) or the pronoun él, se is él with Reflex=Yes, su is DET with Poss=Yes, muy is a form of mucho, and so are their older and spoken spellings, as variants: usté is a form of tú; a demonstrative pronoun with an accent (éste) is a variant of the one without;
  • ser, estar, haber, poder, deber, soler, querer and saber have both AUX and VERB analyses; hay is first of all the verb haber;
  • a participle is a verb with the infinitive as the lemma (VerbForm=Part, Tense=Past) and an adjective with the masculine singular as the lemma (VerbForm=Part without Tense);
  • verbs have no -se in the lemma: quejarse is quejar with the clitic se;
  • the conditional and the imperative have no Tense; a proper name has no features, and its lemma has a capital letter: madrid and Madrid are Madrid, PSOE stays PSOE;
  • an adjective in -ísimo is its own lemma with Degree=Abs.

If the part of speech of a word depends on context, the word has both analyses: que is PRON and SCONJ, la is DET and PRON, a participle is VERB and ADJ. Features: gender, number, person, tense, mood, verb form, degree, negation (Polarity=Neg of no), definiteness (Definite), the type of a pronoun or a determiner (PronType), possessiveness (Poss), reflexivity (Reflex), the case of personal pronouns (Case) and whether they follow a preposition (PrepCase), politeness (Polite=Form of usted), the type of a numeral (NumType) and how it is written (NumForm), and the kind of a sign of punctuation (PunctType, PunctSide).

docs.title: Order of analyses
docs.text:
Analyses go from the most probable to the least. prob is the share of an analysis among the analyses of the word, by how often the treebanks UD Spanish AnCora and GSD have it; for a word they have not seen, the shares are equal and the order is a guess by the ending of the word and the most common features, and a word goes before its older spelling with other accents: á is first of all a, tambien is también. analyze_sentence orders the same analyses by the sentence.

CodeResult 
[(a.lemma, a.pos, round(a.prob, 2)) for a in morph.analyze("casa")][:2]

[('casa', 'NOUN', 0.99), ('casar', 'VERB', 0.01)]

docs.title: Words with clitics
docs.text:
A verb with enclitic pronouns is analyzed as its verb: the analysis describes the infinitive, the gerund or the imperative, and words gives the words of the token, as Universal Dependencies has them. In older and literary writing a finite form takes enclitics too, when the accent of the token marks it: díjole is dijo + le. del and al also have their two words, as do the contractions of de with a pronoun or a demonstrative in older writing: desta is de + esta. A word of the dictionary is not split: comete is a form of cometer, though a few are mostly verbs with clitics: verse is first of all ver + se.

CodeResult 
[(a.lemma, a.pos, a.words, a.source) for a in morph.analyze("dámelo")]

[('dar', 'VERB', ('da', 'me', 'lo'), 'clitics')]

docs.title: Spelling
docs.text:
Case does not matter for finding a word in the dictionary, though a token with a capital letter may also be a name. A word spelled as in the dictionary gives the analyses of that spelling: publico is not público. A word absent as written may be a verb with clitics (verte is ver + te, not verté); otherwise it is looked for without its accents and with a lost diaeresis, and word shows the spelling of the dictionary; for a verb with clitics word is the token as written, in lower case.

CodeResult 
[morph.analyze(word)[0].word for word in ["CAMIÓN", "camion", "pinguino"]]

['camión', 'camión', 'pingüino']

docs.title: Tokens out of the dictionary
docs.text:
A token that the dictionary does not have gets the analyses of rules, with source equal to "rule" and word as written:

  • a sign of punctuation is PUNCT with the PunctType of its signs if they are of one kind, and PunctSide for brackets and question and exclamation marks; a symbol such as %, € or ² is SYM;
  • a number in digits is NUM with NumForm=Digit|NumType=Card, a year too, also with a sign, a fraction, a power or spaces between thousands (-5, 37½, 10², 10 000); the lemma drops the periods between thousands (10.000 is 10000) and a unit after the number (500cc is 500);
  • an ordinal number in digits is ADJ with NumForm=Digit|NumType=Ord, its gender and number, and the masculine singular as the lemma: 2.ª is 2.º;
  • a Roman numeral is NUM with NumForm=Roman, less often a name; in lower case it is a numeral only: xii;
  • a token with a capital letter is a name, PROPN, with itself as the lemma: Josep, CiU, W., TV-3;
  • a link, an email, a hashtag or a mention in lower case is SYM: www.aeat.es, #hola;
  • an abbreviation with a period in lower case that the dictionary does not have is a noun with itself as the lemma (fig.), and so is a lowercase letter (b).

A lowercase abbreviation with a period that the dictionary has without the period gets the nouns and the symbols of that word, with source equal to "dictionary": kg. is kg. A word of the dictionary with a period of another part of speech gets no analyses: come. is a verb with the period of a sentence.

A word with a capital letter that the dictionary knows may be a name too, with its share. An initial (D.) and a word without accents that the dictionary has only with them (Angel, Perez) are mostly names, so their name goes first, while another word with a capital letter is a name less often (Estados, Comisión), so its name usually goes after the analyses of the dictionary. Of the words in capitals, a word of up to four letters is mostly an acronym (ETA, PP), so its name usually goes first, while a longer word and a function word - a preposition, a determiner, a pronoun, a conjunction, an auxiliary - are mostly words of a headline (CAMIONES, EL), so their name usually goes after the analyses of the dictionary. A Roman numeral that the dictionary knows as a word, such as VI, XI or X, is a numeral first. A token with a capital letter that splits as a verb with clitics may be a name too: an imperative without an accent mostly is one (Mandela is first of all PROPN), while an infinitive, a gerund, an imperative with an accent and a finite form mostly are verbs (Hacerlo, Déjame, Levantóse). A lowercase word is a name rarely: miró is first of all mirar, Miró a name. An analysis of a rule has no other forms: forms() gives the analysis itself. is_known tells only the words of the dictionary.

CodeResult 
[(a.lemma, a.pos, a.feats, a.source) for a in morph.analyze("10.000")]
[(a.lemma, a.pos, round(a.prob, 2)) for a in morph.analyze("ETA")]

[('10000', 'NUM', {'NumForm': 'Digit', 'NumType': 'Card'}, 'rule')]
[('ETA', 'PROPN', 0.82), ('eta', 'NOUN', 0.18)]

docs.title: Unknown words
docs.text:
A lowercase word that neither the dictionary nor the rules know gets guessed analyses, with source equal to "guess":

  • a word with a hyphen is analyzed by its last part of an open class or a numeral: palestino-israelíes is a form of palestino-israelí;
  • a word with a known prefix is analyzed by the dictionary word without it, of four letters at least after a prefix of three: supergallos is a form of supergallo, sobreandan of sobreandar;
  • a verb with clitics is analyzed by its guessed gerund, or by its guessed infinitive before se or a clitic of the third person: autogenerarse is autogenerar + se;
  • any other word is analyzed by the dictionary words with the same ending of up to five letters: their parts of speech, features and inflection, by how many words have them and how often AnCora train has their features; a word in -ísimo is an adjective of Degree=Abs: esbeltísima is a form of esbeltísimo.

A guessed word has its forms, guessed too: forms() and inflect() work as for a word of the dictionary. is_known stays false for it.

CodeResult 
[(a.lemma, a.pos, round(a.prob, 2)) for a in morph.analyze("zumbeábamos")]
morph.analyze("zumbeábamos")[0].inflect(Tense="Pres", Person="1", Number="Sing")

[('zumbear', 'VERB', 0.9), ('zumbeábar', 'VERB', 0.09), ('zumbeábar', 'VERB', 0.01)]
'zumbeo'

docs.title: Analyzer
docs.text:
Analyzer(path=None, *, verify=False)

Morphological analyzer: for a word form it finds all analyses in a dictionary built from Wiktionary - the lemma, the part of speech and the Universal Dependencies features - and orders them by probability. A token that the dictionary does not have gets the analyses of rules, and an unknown lowercase word is guessed. The dictionary is loaded when the analyzer is created.

Exceptions:

  • FileNotFoundError - the dictionary file does not exist;
  • OSError - the dictionary file cannot be read: no access, the path points to a directory, a pipe or a device;
  • ValueError - the file is not an esMorph dictionary or is damaged (with verify=True, a deliberately crafted file too), the path has a NUL character;
  • TypeError - a path that is neither a string nor PathLike, verify that is not bool.
CodeResult 
from esmorph import Analyzer

morph = Analyzer()
morph.analyze("hablamos")[0]

Analysis(word='hablamos', lemma='hablar', pos='VERB', feats={'Mood': 'Ind', 'Number': 'Plur', 'Person': '1', 'Tense': 'Pres', 'VerbForm': 'Fin'}, prob=0.978261, words=('hablamos',), source='dictionary')

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
Parameter Type Default Description path str / PathLike None Path to the dictionary file; by default, the dictionary of the package verify bool False Check the whole dictionary, for a file of an untrusted source; takes tens of milliseconds

The object keeps the absolute dictionary path in path of type Path, read-only. The dictionary file is mapped into memory, so processes with the same file share its memory. While an analyzer exists, the file must not be overwritten in place, but it can be replaced with a new file; on Windows an open file can be neither replaced nor deleted. A dictionary is trusted data, like code: loading rejects a damaged file but not every deliberately crafted one, which may make the analysis fail. A dictionary of an untrusted source is loaded with verify=True: a deliberately crafted file is then rejected with ValueError, and pickle keeps the check.

docs.title: Analyses of a word form
docs.text:
analyze · list[Analysis]

analyze(word)

Analyses of the word form, the most probable first; the probabilities sum to 1. Case does not matter for finding the word in the dictionary, though a token with a capital letter may also be a name, and a word absent as written is looked for without its accents and with a lost diaeresis (spelling). A verb with enclitic pronouns is analyzed as its verb (clitics), a token that the dictionary does not have - a sign, a number, a name - by rules, and an unknown lowercase word is guessed. A token that nothing analyzes - with a space or a control character, a lowercase word without a sample such as qzxw - has no analyses.

Parameter Type Default Description word str - Word form

Exceptions:

  • TypeError - a word that is not a string.
CodeResult 
[(a.lemma, a.pos, round(a.prob, 3)) for a in morph.analyze("casa")]
[(a.lemma, a.source) for a in morph.analyze("zumbeábamos")][:1]

[('casa', 'NOUN', 0.986), ('casar', 'VERB', 0.013), ('casar', 'VERB', 0.0)]
[('zumbear', 'guess')]

docs.title: Analyses of a list of word forms
docs.text:
analyze_many · list[list[Analysis]]

analyze_many(words)

Analyses of every word form, as with analyze.

Parameter Type Default Description words Iterable[str] - Word forms: a list, a tuple, a generator

Exceptions:

  • TypeError - a string or bytes instead of a collection of words, a word that is not a string.
CodeResult 
[len(analyses) for analyses in morph.analyze_many(["el", "gato", "come"])]

[2, 1, 2]

docs.title: Analyses of a sentence in context
docs.text:
analyze_sentence · list[list[Analysis]]

analyze_sentence(words)

The analyses of the tokens of a sentence, as analyze gives them, ordered by the context model of the dictionary: the first is the one the model chose by the tokens around, and prob is its score in this sentence. The tokens are those of one sentence in order, as analyze takes them: a contraction (del) or a verb with clitics (dámelo) is one token. A sentence of one token is analyzed as analyze, and one longer than 256 tokens by parts of about 256. The model - a small neural network trained on the treebanks UD Spanish AnCora and GSD - is read on the first call, in a couple of milliseconds; the method releases the GIL.

Parameter Type Default Description words Iterable[str] - Tokens of the sentence: a list, a tuple, a generator

Exceptions:

  • TypeError - a string or bytes instead of a collection of tokens, a token that is not a string;
  • ValueError - the dictionary has no context model.
CodeResult 
sentence = morph.analyze_sentence(["Ella", "la", "vio"])
[(analyses[0].lemma, analyses[0].pos) for analyses in sentence]
[analysis.pos for analysis in morph.analyze("la")]

[('él', 'PRON'), ('él', 'PRON'), ('ver', 'VERB')]
['DET', 'PRON', 'DET', 'NOUN']

docs.title: Lemmatization
docs.text:
lemmatize · list[str]

lemmatize(words)

Lemmas of the most probable analyses of the word forms; a token without analyses comes back in lower case. Equal lemmas are one string object, so the lemmas of a large text take little memory; the method releases the GIL.

Parameter Type Default Description words Iterable[str] - Word forms: a list, a tuple, a generator

Exceptions:

  • TypeError - a string or bytes instead of a collection of words, a word that is not a string.
CodeResult 
morph.lemmatize(["Los", "niños", "cantaban", "canciones"])

['el', 'niño', 'cantar', 'canción']

docs.title: Analysis of a document
docs.text:
annotate · None

annotate(document, *, context=True)

Fills the columns lemma, upos and feats of the words of a document of the anySeg segmenter with the most probable analysis of every word in the context of its sentence, as analyze_sentence orders the analyses of its tokens; with context=False, as analyze orders them, about nine times faster. The earlier values of these columns are replaced. The words of a multiword token are analyzed by the token: dime split into di + me is the imperative of decir with the pronoun me, and clitics after a verb are pronouns. A token that the segmenter leaves as one word gets the analysis of the whole token: devuélvenos is the imperative of devolver. A word without analyses gets its lower case as the lemma and the part of speech X. The method releases the GIL. esMorph does not depend on anySeg: the document is an anyseg.Document or an object with the same column("form"), multiword_tokens (a token has text and words, a word has index), sentences (a sentence has words) and set_columns; an object without sentences is one sentence, and with context=False they are not read.

Parameter Type Default Description document anyseg.Document - Document of the segmenter (pip install anyseg) context bool True Order the analyses by the context model

Exceptions:

  • ValueError - the words of the multiword tokens are not consecutive words of the document in order, the first words of the sentences are not words of the document in order, the analysis is in context and the dictionary has no context model;
  • TypeError - an object that is not a document, a form or the text of a token that is not a string, a token without text or words, a word without index or with an index that is not an integer.
CodeResult 
from anyseg import Segmenter

document = Segmenter("es").segment("Dime la verdad.")
morph.annotate(document)
[(word.form, word.lemma, word.upos) for word in document.words]
document = Segmenter("es").segment("Ella la vio.")
morph.annotate(document, context=False)
document.words[1].upos
morph.annotate(document)
document.words[1].upos

[('Di', 'decir', 'VERB'), ('me', 'yo', 'PRON'), ('la', 'el', 'DET'), ('verdad', 'verdad', 'NOUN'), ('.', '.', 'PUNCT')]
'DET'
'PRON'

docs.title: Dictionary
docs.text:
The dictionary of the package is built from the English Wiktionary of October 2026: 676 thousand word forms of 117 thousand lexemes. Symbols of units (km, kg) come from a table of their own, and determiners, pronouns, prepositions, conjunctions and numerals in words from a table after the treebank UD Spanish AnCora, whose conventions the lemmas and features follow (Word analysis). The probabilities of analyses come from the training parts of UD Spanish AnCora and UD Spanish GSD; word forms they do not have get their order by their ending and the most common features. The dictionary is distributed under the CC BY-SA 4.0 license.

The property dictionary_info describes the dictionary of the analyzer: the source and its snapshot with its SHA-256, the license, the release of Universal Dependencies and the treebanks of the probabilities with their licenses, for a dictionary with a context model the release and the treebanks of its training (context), the number of word forms and the checksum of the file. Every access returns a new dict; its type for type checkers is esmorph.DictionaryInfo, and of context - esmorph.ContextInfo.

CodeResult 
info = morph.dictionary_info
info["source"], info["license"], sorted(info["treebanks"])

('Wiktionary', 'CC BY-SA 4.0', ['UD_Spanish-AnCora', 'UD_Spanish-GSD'])

docs.title: Threads and processes
docs.text:
One analyzer can be used from several threads. lemmatize, analyze_sentence and annotate release the GIL, so threads speed them up. analyze_many creates the analyses as Python objects, so threads speed it up little on any Python, the free-threaded 3.14t included: for a large text, lemmatize or processes are faster. The analyzer and analyses are pickled, so they work with multiprocessing and joblib: processes share the dictionary mapped into memory. Pickling an analysis costs more than finding it, so workers that return lemmas or tuples of fields are faster than workers that return analyses. A pickle keeps the absolute path of the dictionary file (none for the dictionary of the package) and the place of the analysis in the tables of that dictionary, which is looked up anew only with another dictionary: unpickling loads each dictionary once per process, so analyses unpickled one by one share one analyzer, an analysis whose dictionary file is gone or of another version of the format takes the dictionary of the package, and a damaged file raises ValueError. An analysis that the dictionary does not have, as one pickled with another version of it, keeps its fields, but forms() gives an empty list and inflect raises FormNotFoundError.

CodeResult 
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor

texts = [["los", "niños", "cantaban"], ["el", "gato", "come"]]
with ThreadPoolExecutor(2) as pool:
    lemmas = list(pool.map(morph.lemmatize, texts))
lemmas

[['el', 'niño', 'cantar'], ['el', 'gato', 'comer']]

docs.title: The esmorph command
docs.text:
esmorph [options] [file ...]

The command analyzes text from files or the standard input and writes lemmas, parts of speech and Universal Dependencies features in one of four formats. It is installed with the package (pip install esmorph) and also runs as python -m esmorph; without Python, cargo install esmorph --features cli installs it. Every word gets its most probable analysis in the context of its sentence, as annotate gives it: the words of a multiword token are analyzed by the token. The Rust core analyzes and writes in one thread, about 160 thousand tokens per second, and 1.7 million with --no-context.

echo "Dime la verdad del caso." | esmorph

decir yo el verdad de el caso .

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
Option Default Description -f, --format lemmas Output format: lemmas, conllu, tsv, jsonl -i, --input text Input: text, tokens, conllu -d, --dictionary the package dictionary An esMorph dictionary file, checked whole as with verify=True --no-context Order the analyses of a word as analyze does, without the context model: faster; for a list of words and a dictionary without a model -o, --output the standard output The result file; - is the standard output -h, --help Show the help -V, --version Show the version

Files are read one after another; without files and in place of - the standard input is read. The input is in UTF-8: a file in another encoding (Latin-1, cp1252, UTF-16) is not analyzed, unless its first letter with an accent comes after the first 64 KiB: then the text before that line is analyzed up to its last blank line. A single line with invalid bytes is analyzed with U+FFFD in their place. An option value is written separately or attached: -f conllu, -fconllu, --format=conllu. Text is analyzed by paragraphs: a paragraph is written as soon as a blank line or the end of the input closes it - on a terminal at once, and to a pipe or a file whenever the command waits for the next input line, so it can be kept open and fed text paragraph by paragraph. The inputs tokens and conllu are written by sentences.

In Windows PowerShell 5.1 the > redirection and a pipeline (Get-Content text.txt | esmorph) corrupt letters with accents: pass the file as an argument and write the result with the -o option (in PowerShell 7 they work too). Text passed with echo in cmd comes in the console encoding: run chcp 65001 first.

docs.title: Input
docs.text:
• text - text: a blank line ends a paragraph. Tokens, their words and sentences are found by the segmenter anySeg following the conventions of Universal Dependencies: del and al are two words, and so are an infinitive or a gerund with clitics (dárselo) and frequent imperatives (dime). A token that the segmenter leaves as one word gets the analysis of the whole token: devuélvenos is the imperative of devolver. A paragraph longer than 256 KiB is analyzed in pieces that end at a sentence boundary, so memory does not grow with the length of the input; its sentences may then differ slightly from those of the whole text.
  • tokens - one token per line, a blank line separates sentences; separators around the token and everything after a tab are ignored, so a table with the token in the first column works too. A token is one word. A sentence without a blank line is closed after 8,192 tokens. The words around a token change its analysis, so a list of words that do not make a sentence is analyzed with --no-context or with a blank line after every word; the tsv format gives a line per word.
  • conllu - CoNLL-U: the LEMMA, UPOS and FEATS columns are filled, while the other columns, comments, multiword tokens and empty nodes stay as they are. An invalid sentence is written as it is in the conllu format and left out of the others, its line goes to the error message, and the rest of the file is analyzed.
printf '1\tCasas\t_\t_\t_\t_\t0\troot\t_\t_\n2\tblancas\t_\t_\t_\t_\t1\tamod\t_\t_\n' | esmorph -i conllu -f conllu

1   Casas   casa    NOUN    _   Gender=Fem|Number=Plur  0   root    _   _
2   blancas blanco  ADJ _   Gender=Fem|Number=Plur  1   amod    _   _

docs.title: Output formats
docs.text: All formats except jsonl give every word its most probable analysis; jsonl writes all analyses of every token, the most probable first. A word without analyses gets its lower case as the lemma and the part of speech X.

docs.title: lemmas
docs.text: The lemmas of the words of a sentence separated by spaces, a line per sentence; for the text input paragraphs are separated by a blank line.

docs.title: conllu
docs.text:
CoNLL-U as anySeg writes it: multiword tokens with their words, the sent_id and text comments and, for the text input, newdoc at the start of a file, newpar at the start of a paragraph, SpaceAfter=No and SpacesAfter in MISC. The result is the same as annotate of the whole text, except for paragraphs longer than 256 KiB. Analysis gives no syntax tree: from the text and tokens inputs the HEAD and DEPREL columns are _, so a tool that needs a tree, such as the evaluation script of the CoNLL 2018 shared task, reads the result of -i conllu on a file that has one.

echo "Dímelo del mar." | esmorph -f conllu

# newdoc
# newpar
# sent_id = 1
# text = Dímelo del mar.
1-3 Dímelo  _   _   _   _   _   _   _   _
1   Di  decir   VERB    _   Mood=Imp|Number=Sing|Person=2|VerbForm=Fin  _   _   _   _
2   me  yo  PRON    _   Case=Dat|Number=Sing|Person=1|PrepCase=Npr|PronType=Prs _   _   _   _
3   lo  él  PRON    _   Case=Acc|Gender=Masc|Number=Sing|Person=3|PrepCase=Npr|PronType=Prs _   _   _   _
4-5 del _   _   _   _   _   _   _   _
4   de  de  ADP _   _   _   _   _   _
5   el  el  DET _   Definite=Def|Gender=Masc|Number=Sing|PronType=Art   _   _   _   _
6   mar mar NOUN    _   Gender=Masc|Number=Sing _   _   _   SpaceAfter=No
7   .   .   PUNCT   _   PunctType=Peri  _   _   _   _

docs.title: tsv
docs.text:
The word, lemma, part of speech, features and probability of the analysis separated by tabs, without a header (the probability is the score of the context model in the sentence, as analyze_sentence gives it, and with --no-context as analyze gives it); a blank line separates sentences. The probability of a word of a multiword token is its share among the analyses that fit the token: the verb di of dime among the analyses with these words, the clitic la of verla among those of a pronoun.

echo "Dime la verdad." | esmorph -f tsv

Di  decir   VERB    Mood=Imp|Number=Sing|Person=2|VerbForm=Fin  1
me  yo  PRON    Case=Dat|Number=Sing|Person=1|PrepCase=Npr|PronType=Prs 0.45766
la  el  DET Definite=Def|Gender=Fem|Number=Sing|PronType=Art    0.9989243733311355

.   .   PUNCT   PunctType=Peri  1

docs.title: jsonl

docs.title: Exit codes
docs.text:
Code When 0 Success, including when the output is closed before the end (esmorph text.txt \| head) 1 An input file is missing, cannot be read or is not in UTF-8, a line is not in UTF-8 (it is analyzed with U+FFFD), an invalid CoNLL-U sentence; the rest is still analyzed 1 The dictionary cannot be read or is damaged, it has no context model and --no-context is not given, the output file cannot be created, the output file or the standard output is an input file or the dictionary; nothing is analyzed 1 A write error, a closed standard output (the command installed with cargo writes it to /dev/null and ends with 0); the analysis stops 2 Invalid options

Error messages go to the standard error.

docs.title: Comparison
docs.text: esMorph gives all the analyses of a word, the most probable first, and orders them by the sentence with its context model. In context its first analysis has the right part of speech, features and lemma all together for 95.67 % of the words of AnCora, almost as often as spaCy es_core_news_sm trained on it (95.92 %), and more often than spaCy and Stanza on PUD and COSER, new to all of them; its lemma is right more often than that of every other system on AnCora and COSER. Without context its first lemma is right more often than that of simplemma on all three UD test sets, and an analysis with the right part of speech and lemma is among its analyses for 96-99 % of words. It conjugates verbs more accurately than ablaut and verbecc. It analyzes 177 thousand tokens per second in context, 3.5 times faster than spaCy, and 1.9 million without, answers a short text together with loading in 3.0 ms, and every further process with the same dictionary adds 3.6 MB of memory.

docs.title: Quality
docs.text:
The gold standard is the test parts of the UD Spanish AnCora, GSD, PUD and COSER treebanks from the UD 2.18 release: news, web texts, translated Wikipedia sentences and rural speech. Every system gets their words, with del as de and el and a verb apart from its clitics, and esMorph in context gets the tokens of a sentence, a multiword token with its words, as annotate takes a document; punctuation is not counted, and lemmas are compared ignoring case. The lemmas and features of GSD are assigned automatically, so only the part of speech is compared on it. The treebanks follow different conventions, so systems should be compared on the same set rather than sets against each other.

AnCora is the home set of the taggers and of esMorph: spaCy es_core_news_sm is trained on AnCora, the default Stanza model on AnCora and GSD, and esMorph takes its conventions, the frequencies of its analyses and its context model from the training parts of AnCora and GSD. PUD and COSER are new to all of them.

docs.title: Lemma
docs.text:
The share of words with the right lemma, %; for esMorph - the lemma of the first analysis, for a word without analyses - the word in lower case, as lemmatize gives it, and in context - the lemma of the analysis that annotate chooses:

System AnCora PUD COSER esMorph 97.80 97.74 94.49 esMorph in context 99.29 97.71 95.66 simplemma 96.94 96.96 93.50 spaCy es_core_news_sm 98.66 96.69 93.39 Stanza 99.16 97.80 94.98

simplemma gives only a lemma, from a dictionary without parts of speech.

docs.title: Part of speech and features
docs.text:
Taggers and esMorph in context choose the analysis by the sentence; without context the first analysis of esMorph for a word such as que, la or como is the most frequent one. On PUD the analysis without context is right a little more often than in context: the context model learns the conventions of AnCora, and PUD tags the words of names and participles otherwise.

The share of words with the right part of speech, features (gender, number, person, tense, mood, verb form; for names and numerals they are not compared, PUD gives them a gender and a number) and all together with the lemma, %; for esMorph - the first analysis, and the oracle - at least one of its analyses has the right part of speech and lemma:

AnCoraPUDCOSERGSD System Part of speech Features All together Oracle esMorph 92.22 96.14 90.05 98.94 esMorph in context 97.77 97.20 95.67 - spaCy es_core_news_sm 97.12 97.90 95.92 - Stanza 98.57 99.06 97.50 - System Part of speech Features All together Oracle esMorph 91.57 92.06 87.90 97.19 esMorph in context 92.15 90.94 87.52 - spaCy es_core_news_sm 90.31 88.38 83.59 - Stanza 92.94 89.82 86.34 - System Part of speech Features All together Oracle esMorph 90.11 93.25 86.87 96.41 esMorph in context 92.83 94.74 89.76 - spaCy es_core_news_sm 90.00 93.14 85.79 - Stanza 93.60 94.64 89.16 - System Part of speech esMorph 92.43 esMorph in context 92.58 spaCy es_core_news_sm 90.29 Stanza 93.39

docs.title: Inflection
docs.text:
The share of verbs whose form the system gives for their gold lemma and features (infinitive, gerund, participle, mood, tense, person and number), %. Every system gets only the lemma and the features: esMorph is scored by inflect of its verb and auxiliary lexemes of the lemma, one form of each, ablaut and verbecc by any form of the cell of their conjugation table:

System AnCora PUD COSER esMorph 99.65 93.29 95.55 ablaut 98.87 92.71 93.61 verbecc 95.37 92.91 93.53

On AnCora most misses of ablaut and verbecc are the third person singular of the present of haber: ablaut gives only ha and verbecc only hay, while esMorph has both, ha of the auxiliary and hay of the verb; verbecc also fails on pasar, resultar and suceder, which count as misses. On PUD most misses of all three are a convention: the auxiliaries ha and había of compound tenses have Tense=Past; COSER has spoken forms such as trabajao and tá. For the imperfect subjunctive esMorph and ablaut give the form in -ra (fuera), so a form in -se (fuese) is a miss for them.

docs.title: Text analysis
docs.text:
The time to analyze a text together with importing and loading the system in a new process, seconds, both axes on a logarithmic scale:

On a short text almost all the time goes to loading: esMorph answers in 3.0 ms and in 4.9 ms in context, simplemma in 0.33 s, spaCy in 0.81 s, Stanza in 1.7 s. On a long text the analysis speed decides, tokens per second without loading, more is better:

System Tokens per second simplemma, lemmas only 2,455,730 esMorph 1,877,869 esMorph in context 177,200 spaCy es_core_news_sm 50,175 Stanza 3,171

esMorph gives all the analyses of a word, with features and probabilities; its lemmatization alone is almost as fast as simplemma, see Operations. In a spaCy pipeline the component analyzes 112,817 tokens per second, and on the gold words its part of speech, features and lemma are right together for 95.61, 87.51 and 89.56 % of the words of AnCora, PUD and COSER.

docs.title: Operations
docs.text:
Thousands of words, analyses or tables per second, more is better:

Operation esMorph simplemma ablaut verbecc Analysis of a word form: analyze in a loop 1,005 - - - Analysis of a list: analyze_many 1,718 - - - Analysis of sentences in context: analyze_sentence, tokens 157 - - - Lemmatization: lemmatize, lemmatize(word, lang="es") 1,941 2,107 - - Lemmatization in 4 threads: lemmatize 6,541 - - - Form of a noun or an adjective: inflect(Number="Plur") 1,594 - - - Form of a verb: inflect(Mood="Sub", Tense="Pres", Person="1", Number="Sing") 607 - - - Conjugation table: forms(), conjugate(lemma) 116 - 1.7 0.8

simplemma keeps its answers in a cache: with the cache filled by an earlier run over the same words it lemmatizes 4.7 million words per second. ablaut and verbecc build a form only as part of the whole table. lemmatize releases the GIL, so threads sharing one analyzer run in parallel.

docs.title: Loading and memory
docs.text:
esMorph simplemma spaCy es_core_news_sm Stanza Import and loading 3.2 ms 0.38 s 0.95 s 1.9 s Growth of process memory 10.1 MB 131 MB 305 MB 578 MB Every further process 3.6 MB 129 MB 359 MB 1.6 GB

The dictionary file of esMorph is mapped into memory, so multiprocessing or joblib processes and web server workers share it: most of the 10.1 MB of the first process is the dictionary, and every further process adds only its own tables and analyses. The context model is read on the first analysis of a sentence: about 2 ms and 4 MB more.

docs.title: How it was measured
docs.text:
• Quality, inflection and text analysis - the scripts/compare.py script: uv run scripts/compare.py target/compare --chart docs/img/speed.svg. It installs the systems into a separate environment with the versions of all packages pinned in scripts/compare.py.lock (esMorph - the version from it, or a wheel with uv run --with dist/esmorph-*.whl, as for this page), downloads the treebank test parts and the Stanza model with checksum verification before measuring and analyzes the gold words; esMorph in context annotates a document of the gold tokens, with the words of the multiword tokens and the gold sentences, and spaCy with esmorph is spacy.blank("es") with the component alone, a document of the gold words per gold sentence. Inflection - the 5,939, 2,893 and 1,237 verbs of AnCora, PUD and COSER whose lemma is an infinitive, without typos and foreign words.
  • Versions: Python 3.11, esMorph 0.3.0, simplemma 2.0.0, spaCy 3.8.16 with the es_core_news_sm 3.8.0 model without the parser and NER, Stanza 1.15.0 with the default model on the CPU (torch 2.15.0), ablaut 0.11.0, verbecc 2.0.3 (the package has no model and trains one at the first run, so its figures vary by up to 0.2 between installations). Computer - Apple M3 Pro, macOS 26, with other applications running (load average 3-8), so the speeds are an order of magnitude.
  • Text analysis speed - the 53,622 tokens of the AnCora test part with punctuation: tokens per second - the best of two analyses of the whole part after loading, chart points - the best of three runs of importing, loading and analyzing the first 10-50,000 tokens in a new process. Only the call of the system is measured: esMorph analyze_many of all the words and in context annotate of the document, simplemma lemmatize of each word with an empty cache, spaCy nlp.pipe of the sentences, Stanza the whole text; esMorph and simplemma run in one thread, spaCy and Stanza with their default settings.
  • Operations - 47,288 words of the AnCora test part without punctuation, for analyze_sentence its 1,721 sentences of 52,454 tokens with punctuation, a multiword token as one token; the best of three runs in one thread, except the row with threads; verbs - the lexemes of the 4,634 gold verbs whose lemma is an infinitive (verbecc - the first 2,000, one run). Loading and memory - importing, creating the analyzer and the first analysis, the growth of the resident memory of the process (ps -o rss), the median of six runs (of seven for esMorph); a further process - the growth of the memory the process does not share with others (USS), in each of four multiprocessing processes that load the system and analyze 200 sentences.

docs.title: Exceptions
docs.text:
The library raises built-in Python exceptions and one of its own, FormNotFoundError, a subclass of LookupError. It is available from esmorph.

Exception Built-in class When it is raised FormNotFoundError LookupError The lexeme has no form with the requested features, or the dictionary has no lexeme of the analysis (inflect) ValueError - The feature or the value is not in the dictionary (inflect); the file is not an esMorph dictionary or is damaged, with verify=True a deliberately crafted file too, the path has a NUL character (Analyzer); the dictionary has no context model or its model is damaged (analyze_sentence, annotate in context); the words of the multiword tokens are not consecutive words of the document in order, the first words of the sentences are not words of the document in order (annotate) TypeError - An argument of the wrong type: a word or a feature value that is not a string, a string or bytes instead of a collection of words (analyze_many, analyze_sentence, lemmatize), a dictionary path that is neither a string nor PathLike, verify that is not bool (Analyzer); an object that is not a document, a form or the text of a token that is not a string, the index of a word that is not an integer, a sentence without words (annotate) FileNotFoundError OSError The dictionary file does not exist (Analyzer) PermissionError, IsADirectoryError and others OSError The dictionary file cannot be read or is not a file (Analyzer)

Exception messages are in English.

CodeResult 
from esmorph import Analyzer, FormNotFoundError

morph = Analyzer()
try:
    morph.analyze("casa")[0].inflect(Gender="Masc")
except FormNotFoundError as e:
    print(type(e).__name__, isinstance(e, LookupError))
try:
    morph.analyze("gato")[0].inflect(Number="Plural")
except ValueError as e:
    print(e)

FormNotFoundError True
Unknown value of the feature Number: Plural; the dictionary has Plur, Sing

docs.title: Inflection
docs.text: Every analysis knows its lexeme - the forms of the word with the same lemma and part of speech. forms() gives all of them, and inflect() gives the form with the given Universal Dependencies features. The lexeme follows the conventions of the analyses: the auxiliary haber and the verb haber are two lexemes, and so are a participle and the adjective it makes.

docs.title: Forms of the lexeme
docs.text:
forms() returns the forms as analyses like those of analyze, with prob equal to 1. The lemma goes first, then the paradigm: for a verb the infinitive, the gerund, the participles and the finite forms by mood (indicative, conditional, subjunctive, imperative), tense, number and person; for a noun or an adjective by number and gender. Variants - the forms of vos, old and regional spellings - follow the paradigm. An analysis equals its form from forms(): the probability takes no part in the comparison.

CodeResult 
from esmorph import Analyzer

morph = Analyzer()
[form.word for form in morph.analyze("bonitas")[0].forms()]
[form.word for form in morph.analyze("hablamos")[0].forms()][:12]

['bonito', 'bonita', 'bonitos', 'bonitas']
['hablar', 'hablando', 'hablado', 'hablada', 'hablados', 'habladas', 'hablo', 'hablas', 'habla', 'hablamos', 'habláis', 'hablan']

docs.title: Form by features
docs.text:
inflect(**feats) returns the form with the given features as a string. The features that are not given are kept where possible: gatos in the singular is gato, in the feminine gatas. An infinitive or a gerund asked for a tense, a mood, a person or a number gives a finite form.

CodeResult 
gatos = morph.analyze("gatos")[0]
gatos.inflect(Number="Sing"), gatos.inflect(Gender="Fem")
morph.analyze("hablar")[0].inflect(Tense="Past", Person="3", Number="Plur")

('gato', 'gatas')
'hablaron'

Several forms may have the same features. A variant comes only from a variant: hablás in the imperative is hablá, while hablas is habla. A variant of a noun, an adjective, a determiner or a pronoun still gives a main form closer in spelling than its variants: buen in the plural is buenos, not the older bones. Of the two forms of the imperfect subjunctive the analysis keeps its own: hablase in the first person plural is hablásemos. Otherwise a form that the treebanks have clearly more often goes first (the verb haber gives hay, the auxiliary gives ha), and the order of the table of the word decides the rest: ser gives soy, not seigo. A form of some countries only is a variant: the feminine participle of apagar is apagada, not apaga.

CodeResult 
[(a.pos, a.inflect(Person="3", Number="Sing")) for a in morph.analyze("haber")[:2]]

[('AUX', 'ha'), ('VERB', 'hay')]

A form of a noun, a name, an adjective, a determiner, a pronoun or a numeral without a gender or a number agrees with any: grande in the feminine plural is grandes, and an analysis of a rule stays itself (ETA). Of the forms that keep equally many features of the analysis, a form that changes another feature goes after one that lacks it, and a form with the gender and number of the analysis before one without them: chulitos in the singular is chulito, lo in the dative is le, sí in the dative is se, and ustedes, which has no gender, stays ustedes in the feminine. A value with several parts, such as Case=Acc,Nom, may be given in any order. A verb with clitics inflects as its verb, and its forms have no clitics: dámelo in the plural is dad.

CodeResult 
grande, token = morph.analyze("grande")[0], morph.analyze("dámelo")[0]
grande.inflect(Gender="Fem", Number="Plur"), token.inflect(Number="Plur")

('grandes', 'dad')

docs.title: Errors
docs.text:
• FormNotFoundError, a subclass of LookupError - the lexeme has no form with these features: casa has no masculine; or the dictionary has no lexeme of the analysis, as one pickled with another version of it;
  • ValueError - the dictionary has no such feature or value, as in Number="Plural"; the message lists the valid ones;
  • TypeError - a value is not a string.
CodeResult 
from esmorph import FormNotFoundError

try:
    morph.analyze("casa")[0].inflect(Gender="Masc")
except FormNotFoundError as error:
    print(error)

The lexeme of 'casa' has no form Gender=Masc

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
Python 3.11 or newer is required.

pip install esmorph

The package also installs the esmorph command. The extra spacy installs spaCy for the esmorph component: pip install "esmorph[spacy]".

docs.title: Prebuilt wheels
docs.text:
PyPI hosts wheels for Linux (x86_64 and aarch64, manylinux and musllinux), macOS (Intel and Apple Silicon) and Windows (x64 and arm64). One wheel serves every Python version starting with 3.11, and the free-threaded Python 3.14t has a wheel of its own; Rust is not needed to install them. The dictionary is part of the package and needs no separate installation. The free-threaded Python 3.13 is not supported: free-threaded builds start with 3.14.

Pre-release versions X.Y.Z.devN are published only on TestPyPI:

pip install --index-url https://test.pypi.org/simple/ --extra-index-url https://pypi.org/simple/ --pre esmorph

uv takes a package from the first index that has it, so it needs another order of indexes:

uv pip install --extra-index-url https://test.pypi.org/simple/ --index-strategy unsafe-best-match --pre esmorph

docs.title: Building from source
docs.text:
On other platforms and on free-threaded builds newer than 3.14 pip builds the package from source, which requires Rust 1.88 or newer:

curl --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 -sSf https://sh.rustup.rs | sh
pip install esmorph

The development environment is described in CONTRIBUTING.md.

docs.title: Rust
docs.text:
The analyzer core is published on crates.io as the esmorph crate and the dictionary as the esmorph-dict-es crate: it is enabled by default through the feature bundled and loaded with Dictionary::bundled(). The API documentation is on docs.rs.

cargo add esmorph

The feature anyseg adds Dictionary::annotate for documents of the segmenter anySeg, and the feature cli adds the esmorph command, which installs without Python:

cargo install esmorph --features cli

docs.title: spaCy
docs.text:
The esmorph component plugs esMorph into a spaCy pipeline: it annotates the tokens of a document with the part of speech (pos_), the Universal Dependencies features (morph) and the lemma (lemma_) of the analysis in context. In a pipeline it replaces the tagger, the morphologizer and the lemmatizer.

pip install "esmorph[spacy]"

The component registers with spaCy when the package is installed and is added by name, without importing esmorph. spaCy has no prebuilt wheels for Python 3.14t without the GIL.

CodeResult 
import spacy

nlp = spacy.blank("es")
_ = nlp.add_pipe("esmorph")
doc = nlp("Ella la vio del balcón.")
[(token.lemma_, token.pos_) for token in doc]
str(doc[1].morph)

[('él', 'PRON'), ('él', 'PRON'), ('ver', 'VERB'), ('de', 'ADP'), ('balcón', 'NOUN'), ('.', 'PUNCT')]
'Case=Acc|Gender=Fem|Number=Sing|Person=3|PrepCase=Npr|PronType=Prs'

On the gold words of the test parts of the treebanks (Comparison) the part of speech, features and lemma of the component are right together for 95.61, 87.51 and 89.56 % of the words of AnCora, PUD and COSER, against 95.92, 83.59 and 85.79 % of es_core_news_sm, and a pipeline of the component alone analyzes 113 thousand tokens per second against 50 thousand.

docs.title: es_core_news models
docs.text:
In a pipeline of the es_core_news_* models the component replaces the morphologizer and the lemmatizer, while the parser and named entity recognition stay; the component takes the sentences the parser marks and goes before attribute_ruler, which fills tag_ by the part of speech. The morphologizer is a small layer over the vectors of tok2vec, which the parser needs anyway, and the lemmatizer is rules and tables, so the component makes such a pipeline about 15 % slower.

nlp = spacy.load("es_core_news_sm", exclude=["morphologizer", "lemmatizer"])
nlp.add_pipe("esmorph", before="attribute_ruler")

docs.title: Tokens of several words
docs.text: A spaCy token is a token of the text: a contraction (del, al) or a verb with clitics (dámelo) is one token. It gets the analysis of its first word: del is ADP de, dámelo is VERB dar in the imperative. With the tokenizer of anySeg, which gives the words of a token, it is the most probable analysis with these words, as annotate chooses it, and with another tokenizer the most probable analysis of the token in the sentence. The words of the token are in its esMorph analysis.

docs.title: Sentences
docs.text:
The context model analyzes a whole sentence. The component takes the sentences from the annotation of the document - the parser, senter or sentencizer, and without it splits the document after the tokens of sentence end marks («.», «!», «?», «…») with the closing quotes and brackets right after them, and at a blank line. Whitespace tokens and tokens of invisible separators only (BOM, U+200B, U+2060, the soft hyphen) get the part of speech SPACE, as in spaCy models, and the token itself as the lemma: the model does not see them. A token without an analysis of esMorph gets X and the token in lower case as the lemma, as in the esmorph command.

Tokens, their words and sentence starts by the conventions of Universal Dependencies, on which the context model is trained, come from the segmenter anySeg (pip install "anyseg[spacy]"): the tokenizer anyseg.Tokenizer.v1 and the component anyseg_sentencizer go before esmorph. The words of a token of several are then also in token._.anyseg_words.

CodeResult 
tokenizer = {"@tokenizers": "anyseg.Tokenizer.v1"}
nlp = spacy.blank("es", config={"nlp": {"tokenizer": tokenizer}})
_ = nlp.add_pipe("anyseg_sentencizer")
_ = nlp.add_pipe("esmorph")
[(token.text, token.lemma_) for token in nlp("Dámelo ya, Sr. García.")]

[('Dámelo', 'dar'), ('ya', 'ya'), (',', ','), ('Sr.', 'Sr.'), ('García', 'García'), ('.', '.')]

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
Parameter Type Default Description dictionary str None Path to the dictionary file; by default - the dictionary of the package context bool True Choose the analysis by the tokens around; False - the most probable analysis of the word form, as with analyze

nlp.evaluate and spacy evaluate score the component as the morphologizer and the lemmatizer: pos_acc, morph_acc, morph_per_feat and lemma_acc. spacy package does not find esmorph among the requirements of a pipeline: add "requirements": ["esmorph>=0.3,<0.4"] to its meta.json before packaging. The parameter dictionary keeps a path, so a dictionary of its own must be at that path where the package is installed.

CodeResult 
nlp = spacy.blank("es")
_ = nlp.add_pipe("esmorph", config={"context": False})
[(token.lemma_, token.pos_) for token in nlp("Ella la vio")]

[('él', 'PRON'), ('el', 'DET'), ('ver', 'VERB')]

docs.title: esMorph analysis
docs.text:
token._.esmorph is the esMorph analysis with the lemma, the part of speech and the features of the token, by the dictionary of the component that annotated the document: it gives the words of the token and the forms of the word. Its probability does not take the context into account. If the word form has no such analysis - for example, another component changed the annotation of the token - the value is None. A document keeps the path of a dictionary other than the one of the package in user_data, so DocBin(store_user_data=True) and span.as_doc(copy_user_data=True) preserve it, while Doc.from_docs does not carry it over.

CodeResult 
nlp = spacy.blank("es")
_ = nlp.add_pipe("esmorph")
analysis = nlp("Dámelo ya")[0]._.esmorph
analysis.lemma, analysis.words
analysis.inflect(Mood="Ind", Tense="Pres", Person="1")

('dar', ('da', 'me', 'lo'))
'doy'

docs.title: esMorph
docs.text:
esMorph es un analizador morfológico del español: un núcleo en Rust con API para Python. Para una forma de palabra el analizador busca sus análisis en un diccionario creado a partir de Wiktionary - el lema, la categoría gramatical y los rasgos de Universal Dependencies -, los ordena por probabilidad y construye las formas de la palabra: conjugación, género y número.

Versión temprana

Hasta la 1.0 la API puede cambiar entre versiones 0.x; los cambios se describen en las notas de cada versión.

docs.title: Funciones
docs.text:
• Análisis

    Lema, categoría y rasgos de UD, probabilidad del análisis; el análisis de una oración en contexto, listas de palabras, lematización y documentos del segmentador anySeg sin el GIL

    Analizador

  • Universal Dependencies

    Categorías, rasgos y lemas según las directrices de UD y las convenciones de AnCora; verbos con clíticos, números, signos y nombres por reglas, palabras desconocidas por su terminación

    Análisis de palabras

  • Flexión

    Formas del lexema y la forma según rasgos de UD: conjugación, género y número

    Flexión

  • Línea de comandos

    El comando esmorph: lemas, CoNLL-U, TSV o JSON Lines de archivos de texto, tokens o CoNLL-U

    El comando esmorph

  • spaCy

    El componente esmorph: el análisis en contexto en lugar del etiquetador, el morfologizador y el lematizador de una cadena

    spaCy

  • Comparación

    Precisión, flexión y velocidad frente a simplemma, spaCy, Stanza, ablaut y verbecc, carga y memoria

    Comparación

  • Excepciones

    Excepciones integradas de Python y FormNotFoundError para las formas que faltan

    Excepciones

docs.title: Instalación
docs.text:
Se requiere Python 3.11 o superior.

pip install esmorph

Los paquetes precompilados, la compilación desde el código fuente y el crate de Rust se describen en la página de instalación.

docs.title: Inicio rápido
docs.text:
CódigoResultado 
from esmorph import Analyzer

morph = Analyzer()
morph.lemmatize(["Los", "niños", "cantaban", "canciones"])
[(a.lemma, a.pos, round(a.prob, 3)) for a in morph.analyze("casa")][:2]
morph.analyze("gatos")[0].inflect(Gender="Fem")
morph.analyze("hablar")[0].inflect(Tense="Past", Person="3", Number="Plur")

['el', 'niño', 'cantar', 'canción']
[('casa', 'NOUN', 0.986), ('casar', 'VERB', 0.013)]
'gatas'
'hablaron'
Estructura del proyecto
  • crates/esmorph - el núcleo del analizador en Rust: formato del diccionario, construcción, análisis, reglas, estimación y flexión
  • crates/esmorph-build - la construcción del diccionario a partir de la exportación de Wiktionary y los recuentos de los treebanks
  • crates/esmorph-dict-es - el crate con el diccionario para esmorph en crates.io
  • crates/esmorph-py - el módulo de Python esmorph._esmorph sobre PyO3
  • python/esmorph - el paquete de Python
  • scripts - la exportación de Wiktionary y de los recuentos de los treebanks, las convenciones del diccionario, el entrenamiento del modelo de contexto, la comprobación del paquete instalado antes de publicar y la comparación con otras herramientas
  • data - las tablas de clases cerradas según UD Spanish AnCora y de los símbolos de unidades, los pesos del modelo de contexto
  • docs - documentación de MkDocs en inglés y español
  • tests - pruebas del paquete de Python

docs.title: Análisis de palabras
docs.text:
Un análisis es un objeto Analysis que devuelven los métodos analyze y analyze_many del analizador: el lema, la categoría gramatical y los rasgos de Universal Dependencies, la probabilidad, las palabras del token y la fuente del análisis. Los análisis son inmutables; se pueden comparar (la probabilidad no participa en la comparación, así que un análisis es igual a su forma de forms()), poner en conjuntos y serializar con pickle. Las formas de una palabra las dan los métodos forms e inflect - véase Flexión.

CódigoResultado 
from esmorph import Analyzer

morph = Analyzer()
analysis = morph.analyze("cantaban")[0]
analysis.word, analysis.lemma, analysis.pos, analysis.feats, analysis.words, analysis.source

('cantaban',
 'cantar',
 'VERB',
 {'Mood': 'Ind', 'Number': 'Plur', 'Person': '3', 'Tense': 'Imp', 'VerbForm': 'Fin'},
 ('cantaban',),
 'dictionary')

docs.title: Atributos
docs.text: Atributo Tipo Descripción word str La forma de palabra tal como la escribe el diccionario, con sus tildes; un verbo con clíticos tal como está escrito, en minúsculas; un token de las reglas tal como está escrito, sin caracteres invisibles, con las marcas combinantes unidas a sus letras y con - en lugar de los guiones U+2010 y U+2011 lemma str El lema pos str Categoría gramatical de UD: NOUN, VERB, ADJ, DET, ADP, etc. feats dict[str, str] Rasgos de UD: {"Gender": "Fem", "Number": "Plur"}; un diccionario nuevo cada vez, cambiarlo no cambia el análisis prob float Parte del análisis entre los análisis de la palabra; la suma de todos es 1. En analyze_sentence - la puntuación del modelo de contexto en la oración words tuple[str, ...] Palabras del token: un verbo y sus clíticos, las palabras de una contracción (del, al, la antigua desta) o la propia palabra; el análisis describe la primera source str De dónde viene el análisis: "dictionary" - la forma está en el diccionario, "clitics" - un verbo del diccionario con clíticos, "rule" - un análisis por regla, "guess" - un análisis estimado de una palabra desconocida

docs.title: Categorías y rasgos
docs.text:
Las categorías gramaticales, los rasgos y los lemas siguen las directrices de Universal Dependencies y, donde estas callan, las convenciones del mayor treebank del español, UD Spanish AnCora, así que el resultado se puede comparar con spaCy, Stanza y otras herramientas de UD:

  • los determinantes, los pronombres, las preposiciones y las conjunciones tienen los lemas y los rasgos de AnCora: la es el artículo el (Definite=Def, PronType=Art) o el pronombre él, se es él con Reflex=Yes, su es DET con Poss=Yes, muy es una forma de mucho, y lo mismo sus grafías antiguas y orales, como variantes: usté es una forma de tú; un pronombre demostrativo con tilde (éste) es una variante del que no la lleva;
  • ser, estar, haber, poder, deber, soler, querer y saber tienen análisis AUX y VERB; hay es ante todo el verbo haber;
  • un participio es un verbo con el infinitivo como lema (VerbForm=Part, Tense=Past) y un adjetivo con el masculino singular como lema (VerbForm=Part sin Tense);
  • los verbos no llevan -se en el lema: quejarse es quejar con el clítico se;
  • el condicional y el imperativo no tienen Tense; un nombre propio no tiene rasgos, y su lema lleva mayúscula: madrid y Madrid son Madrid, PSOE sigue siendo PSOE;
  • un adjetivo en -ísimo es su propio lema con Degree=Abs.

Si la categoría de una palabra depende del contexto, la palabra tiene ambos análisis: que es PRON y SCONJ, la es DET y PRON, un participio es VERB y ADJ. Rasgos: género, número, persona, tiempo, modo, forma verbal, grado, negación (Polarity=Neg de no), definitud (Definite), el tipo de pronombre o de determinante (PronType), la posesión (Poss), la reflexividad (Reflex), el caso de los pronombres personales (Case) y si van tras una preposición (PrepCase), la cortesía (Polite=Form de usted), el tipo de numeral (NumType) y cómo se escribe (NumForm), y la clase de un signo de puntuación (PunctType, PunctSide).

docs.title: Orden de los análisis
docs.text:
Los análisis van del más probable al menos probable. prob es la parte de un análisis entre los análisis de la palabra, según la frecuencia con que lo tienen los treebanks UD Spanish AnCora y GSD; para una palabra que no han visto, las partes son iguales y el orden se estima por la terminación de la palabra y los rasgos más comunes, y una palabra va antes que su grafía antigua con otras tildes: á es ante todo a, tambien es también. analyze_sentence ordena los mismos análisis por la oración.

CódigoResultado 
[(a.lemma, a.pos, round(a.prob, 2)) for a in morph.analyze("casa")][:2]

[('casa', 'NOUN', 0.99), ('casar', 'VERB', 0.01)]

docs.title: Palabras con clíticos
docs.text:
Un verbo con pronombres enclíticos se analiza como su verbo: el análisis describe el infinitivo, el gerundio o el imperativo, y words da las palabras del token, como las tiene Universal Dependencies. En la escritura antigua y literaria una forma personal también lleva enclíticos, si la tilde del token la marca: díjole es dijo + le. del y al también tienen sus dos palabras, como las contracciones de de con un pronombre o un demostrativo en la escritura antigua: desta es de + esta. Una palabra del diccionario no se divide: comete es una forma de cometer, aunque unas pocas suelen ser verbos con clíticos: verse es ante todo ver + se.

CódigoResultado 
[(a.lemma, a.pos, a.words, a.source) for a in morph.analyze("dámelo")]

[('dar', 'VERB', ('da', 'me', 'lo'), 'clitics')]

docs.title: Ortografía
docs.text:
Las mayúsculas no importan para buscar una palabra en el diccionario, aunque un token con mayúscula también puede ser un nombre. Una palabra escrita como en el diccionario da los análisis de esa grafía: publico no es público. Una palabra que no está tal como se escribe puede ser un verbo con clíticos (verte es ver + te, no verté); si no lo es, se busca sin sus tildes y con la diéresis perdida, y word muestra la grafía del diccionario; para un verbo con clíticos word es el token tal como se escribe, en minúsculas.

CódigoResultado 
[morph.analyze(word)[0].word for word in ["CAMIÓN", "camion", "pinguino"]]

['camión', 'camión', 'pingüino']

docs.title: Tokens fuera del diccionario
docs.text:
Un token que el diccionario no tiene recibe los análisis de unas reglas, con source igual a "rule" y word tal como está escrito:

  • un signo de puntuación es PUNCT con el PunctType de sus signos si son de una misma clase, y PunctSide para los paréntesis, los corchetes, las llaves y los signos de interrogación y de exclamación; un símbolo como %, € o ² es SYM;
  • un número en cifras es NUM con NumForm=Digit|NumType=Card, también un año, también con signo, fracción, potencia o espacios entre los millares (-5, 37½, 10², 10 000); el lema quita los puntos entre los millares (10.000 es 10000) y una unidad tras el número (500cc es 500);
  • un número ordinal en cifras es ADJ con NumForm=Digit|NumType=Ord, su género y su número, y el masculino singular como lema: 2.ª es 2.º;
  • un número romano es NUM con NumForm=Roman, con menos frecuencia un nombre; en minúsculas es solo un numeral: xii;
  • un token con una letra mayúscula es un nombre, PROPN, con él mismo como lema: Josep, CiU, W., TV-3;
  • un enlace, un correo, una etiqueta o una mención en minúsculas es SYM: www.aeat.es, #hola;
  • una abreviatura con punto en minúsculas que el diccionario no tiene es un sustantivo con ella misma como lema (fig.), y lo mismo una letra minúscula (b).

Una abreviatura con punto en minúsculas que el diccionario tiene sin el punto recibe los sustantivos y los símbolos de esa palabra, con source igual a "dictionary": kg. es kg. Una palabra del diccionario de otra categoría con un punto no recibe análisis: come. es un verbo con el punto de una oración.

Una palabra con mayúscula que el diccionario conoce también puede ser un nombre, con su parte. Una inicial (D.) y una palabra sin tildes que el diccionario solo tiene con ellas (Angel, Perez) suelen ser nombres, así que su nombre va primero, mientras que otra palabra con mayúscula es un nombre con menos frecuencia (Estados, Comisión), así que su nombre suele ir después de los análisis del diccionario. De las palabras en mayúsculas, una palabra de hasta cuatro letras suele ser una sigla (ETA, PP), así que su nombre suele ir primero, mientras que una palabra más larga y una palabra funcional - una preposición, un determinante, un pronombre, una conjunción, un auxiliar - suelen ser palabras de un titular (CAMIONES, EL), así que su nombre suele ir después de los análisis del diccionario. Un número romano que el diccionario conoce como palabra, como VI, XI o X, es ante todo un numeral. Un token con mayúscula que se divide en un verbo con clíticos también puede ser un nombre: un imperativo sin tilde suele serlo (Mandela es ante todo PROPN), mientras que un infinitivo, un gerundio, un imperativo con tilde y una forma personal suelen ser verbos (Hacerlo, Déjame, Levantóse). Una palabra en minúsculas rara vez es un nombre: miró es ante todo mirar, Miró es un nombre. Un análisis de una regla no tiene otras formas: forms() da el propio análisis. is_known solo indica las palabras del diccionario.

CódigoResultado 
[(a.lemma, a.pos, a.feats, a.source) for a in morph.analyze("10.000")]
[(a.lemma, a.pos, round(a.prob, 2)) for a in morph.analyze("ETA")]

[('10000', 'NUM', {'NumForm': 'Digit', 'NumType': 'Card'}, 'rule')]
[('ETA', 'PROPN', 0.82), ('eta', 'NOUN', 0.18)]

docs.title: Palabras desconocidas
docs.text:
Una palabra en minúsculas que ni el diccionario ni las reglas conocen recibe análisis estimados, con source igual a "guess":

  • una palabra con guion se analiza por su última parte de una clase abierta o un numeral: palestino-israelíes es una forma de palestino-israelí;
  • una palabra con un prefijo conocido se analiza por la palabra del diccionario sin él, de cuatro letras al menos tras un prefijo de tres: supergallos es una forma de supergallo, sobreandan de sobreandar;
  • un verbo con clíticos se analiza por su gerundio estimado, o por su infinitivo estimado ante se o un clítico de tercera persona: autogenerarse es autogenerar + se;
  • cualquier otra palabra se analiza por las palabras del diccionario con la misma terminación de hasta cinco letras: sus categorías, rasgos y flexión, según cuántas palabras los tienen y con qué frecuencia AnCora train tiene sus rasgos; una palabra en -ísimo es un adjetivo de Degree=Abs: esbeltísima es una forma de esbeltísimo.

Una palabra estimada tiene sus formas, también estimadas: forms() e inflect() funcionan como con una palabra del diccionario. is_known sigue siendo falso para ella.

CódigoResultado 
[(a.lemma, a.pos, round(a.prob, 2)) for a in morph.analyze("zumbeábamos")]
morph.analyze("zumbeábamos")[0].inflect(Tense="Pres", Person="1", Number="Sing")

[('zumbear', 'VERB', 0.9), ('zumbeábar', 'VERB', 0.09), ('zumbeábar', 'VERB', 0.01)]
'zumbeo'

docs.title: Analizador
docs.text:
Analyzer(path=None, *, verify=False)

Analizador morfológico: para una forma de palabra busca todos sus análisis en un diccionario creado a partir de Wiktionary - el lema, la categoría gramatical y los rasgos de Universal Dependencies - y los ordena por probabilidad. Un token que el diccionario no tiene recibe los análisis de unas reglas, y una palabra desconocida en minúsculas se estima. El diccionario se carga al crear el analizador.

Excepciones:

  • FileNotFoundError - el archivo del diccionario no existe;
  • OSError - el archivo del diccionario no se puede leer: sin acceso, la ruta es un directorio, una tubería o un dispositivo;
  • ValueError - el archivo no es un diccionario de esMorph o está dañado (con verify=True, también un archivo creado a propósito), la ruta tiene un carácter NUL;
  • TypeError - una ruta que no es una cadena ni PathLike, verify que no es bool.
CódigoResultado 
from esmorph import Analyzer

morph = Analyzer()
morph.analyze("hablamos")[0]

Analysis(word='hablamos', lemma='hablar', pos='VERB', feats={'Mood': 'Ind', 'Number': 'Plur', 'Person': '1', 'Tense': 'Pres', 'VerbForm': 'Fin'}, prob=0.978261, words=('hablamos',), source='dictionary')

docs.title: Parámetros
docs.text:
Parámetro Tipo Por defecto Descripción path str / PathLike None Ruta al archivo del diccionario; por defecto, el diccionario del paquete verify bool False Comprobar el diccionario entero, para un archivo de una fuente no fiable; tarda decenas de milisegundos

El objeto guarda la ruta absoluta del diccionario en path, de tipo Path y solo de lectura. El archivo del diccionario se proyecta en memoria, así que los procesos con el mismo archivo comparten su memoria. Mientras exista un analizador, el archivo no debe sobrescribirse en su lugar, pero se puede sustituir por un archivo nuevo; en Windows un archivo abierto no se puede ni sustituir ni borrar. Un diccionario es un dato de confianza, como el código: la carga rechaza un archivo dañado, pero no todo archivo creado a propósito, que puede hacer fallar el análisis. Un diccionario de una fuente no fiable se carga con verify=True: entonces un archivo creado a propósito se rechaza con ValueError, y pickle conserva la comprobación.

docs.title: Análisis de una forma de palabra
docs.text:
analyze · list[Analysis]

analyze(word)

Los análisis de la forma de palabra, primero el más probable; las probabilidades suman 1. Las mayúsculas no importan para buscar la palabra en el diccionario, aunque un token con mayúscula también puede ser un nombre, y una palabra que no está tal como se escribe se busca sin sus tildes y con una diéresis perdida (ortografía). Un verbo con pronombres enclíticos se analiza como su verbo (clíticos), un token que el diccionario no tiene - un signo, un número, un nombre - por reglas, y una palabra desconocida en minúsculas se estima. Un token que nada analiza - con un espacio o un carácter de control, una palabra en minúsculas sin modelo como qzxw - no tiene análisis.

Parámetro Tipo Por defecto Descripción word str - Forma de palabra

Excepciones:

  • TypeError - una palabra que no es una cadena.
CódigoResultado 
[(a.lemma, a.pos, round(a.prob, 3)) for a in morph.analyze("casa")]
[(a.lemma, a.source) for a in morph.analyze("zumbeábamos")][:1]

[('casa', 'NOUN', 0.986), ('casar', 'VERB', 0.013), ('casar', 'VERB', 0.0)]
[('zumbear', 'guess')]

docs.title: Análisis de una lista de formas
docs.text:
analyze_many · list[list[Analysis]]

analyze_many(words)

Los análisis de cada forma de palabra, como con analyze.

Parámetro Tipo Por defecto Descripción words Iterable[str] - Formas de palabra: una lista, una tupla, un generador

Excepciones:

  • TypeError - una cadena o bytes en lugar de una colección de palabras, una palabra que no es una cadena.
CódigoResultado 
[len(analyses) for analyses in morph.analyze_many(["el", "gato", "come"])]

[2, 1, 2]

docs.title: Análisis de una oración en contexto
docs.text:
analyze_sentence · list[list[Analysis]]

analyze_sentence(words)

Los análisis de los tokens de una oración, tal como los da analyze, ordenados por el modelo de contexto del diccionario: el primero es el que el modelo eligió por los tokens de alrededor, y prob es su puntuación en esta oración. Los tokens son los de una oración en orden, tal como los toma analyze: una contracción (del) o un verbo con clíticos (dámelo) es un solo token. Una oración de un token se analiza como con analyze, y una de más de 256 tokens, por partes de unos 256. El modelo - una pequeña red neuronal entrenada con los treebanks UD Spanish AnCora y GSD - se lee en la primera llamada, en un par de milisegundos; el método libera el GIL.

Parámetro Tipo Por defecto Descripción words Iterable[str] - Tokens de la oración: una lista, una tupla, un generador

Excepciones:

  • TypeError - una cadena o bytes en lugar de una colección de tokens, un token que no es una cadena;
  • ValueError - el diccionario no tiene modelo de contexto.
CódigoResultado 
sentence = morph.analyze_sentence(["Ella", "la", "vio"])
[(analyses[0].lemma, analyses[0].pos) for analyses in sentence]
[analysis.pos for analysis in morph.analyze("la")]

[('él', 'PRON'), ('él', 'PRON'), ('ver', 'VERB')]
['DET', 'PRON', 'DET', 'NOUN']

docs.title: Lematización
docs.text:
lemmatize · list[str]

lemmatize(words)

Los lemas de los análisis más probables de las formas de palabra; un token sin análisis vuelve en minúsculas. Los lemas iguales son un mismo objeto de cadena, así que los lemas de un texto grande ocupan poca memoria; el método libera el GIL.

Parámetro Tipo Por defecto Descripción words Iterable[str] - Formas de palabra: una lista, una tupla, un generador

Excepciones:

  • TypeError - una cadena o bytes en lugar de una colección de palabras, una palabra que no es una cadena.
CódigoResultado 
morph.lemmatize(["Los", "niños", "cantaban", "canciones"])

['el', 'niño', 'cantar', 'canción']

docs.title: Análisis de un documento
docs.text:
annotate · None

annotate(document, *, context=True)

Rellena las columnas lemma, upos y feats de las palabras de un documento del segmentador anySeg con el análisis más probable de cada palabra en el contexto de su oración, en el orden en que analyze_sentence ordena los análisis de sus tokens; con context=False, en el orden de analyze, unas nueve veces más rápido. Los valores anteriores de estas columnas se sustituyen. Las palabras de un token multipalabra se analizan por el token: dime dividido en di + me es el imperativo de decir con el pronombre me, y los clíticos tras un verbo son pronombres. Un token que el segmentador deja como una sola palabra recibe el análisis del token entero: devuélvenos es el imperativo de devolver. Una palabra sin análisis recibe como lema su forma en minúsculas y la categoría X. El método libera el GIL. esMorph no depende de anySeg: el documento es un anyseg.Document o un objeto con los mismos column("form"), multiword_tokens (un token tiene text y words, una palabra tiene index), sentences (una oración tiene words) y set_columns; un objeto sin sentences es una sola oración, y con context=False no se leen.

Parámetro Tipo Por defecto Descripción document anyseg.Document - Documento del segmentador (pip install anyseg) context bool True Ordenar los análisis con el modelo de contexto

Excepciones:

  • ValueError - las palabras de los tokens multipalabra no son palabras consecutivas del documento en orden, las primeras palabras de las oraciones no son palabras del documento en orden, el análisis es en contexto y el diccionario no tiene modelo de contexto;
  • TypeError - un objeto que no es un documento, una forma o el texto de un token que no es una cadena, un token sin text o words, una palabra sin index o con un índice que no es un entero.

from anyseg import Segmenter

document = Segmenter("es").segment("Dime la verdad.")
morph.annotate(document)
[(word.form, word.lemma, word.upos) for word in document.words]
document = Segmenter("es").segment("Ella la vio.")
morph.annotate(document, context=False)
document.words[1].upos
morph.annotate(document)
document.words[1].upos
